newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-METZ HOPE TO EXPLOIT MONACO'S CONFIDENCE CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-METZ HOPE TO EXPLOIT MONACO'S CONFIDENCE CRISIS.

text.p: Metz could take advantage of doubts in the Monaco camp when they entertain the leaders in the French first division on Saturday.
Monaco, so solid in the league this year, were bundled out of the League Cup semifinals 2-1 at Strasbourg on Tuesday.
"I'm sorry for the people close to the club because a final and another possible trophy does one good," said France defender and Monaco captain Patrick Blondeau.
"But there were choices, players who did not play and we're not happy because it mattered to us," he added in remarks that smacked of criticism of coach Jean Tigana.
"To leave first-choice players on the bench was to take risks and the result was this elimination which disappoints me a lot."
Tigana, who was unhappy with the way Monaco conceded the first goal from a favourite Strasbourg set piece, defended his strategy.
"I have a squad and all the players have to play. I've always said you have to rotate the group and I merely brought back three players who were first choice at the start of the season," he said.
Defender Eric Di Meco made his first start in more than five months after injury, while midfielder Enzo Scifo and striker Dan Petersen also started the match.
But Tigana kept his best strikers Anderson and Victor Ikpeba on the bench until early in the second half.
"Let's think about Metz now and the very hard match we can expect there because they have their eyes on (a place in) Europe and they're going to give their all," Tigana said.

Monaco are a comfortable seven points ahead of second-placed Paris St Germain but they cannot afford another setback as they prepare to meet Newcastle United in the UEFA Cup quarter-finals next month.
They have defender Martin Djetou in doubt, while Scotland's John Collins, captain Franck Dumas and midfielder Gilles Grimandi are back in the squad after missing the midweek trip to Strasbourg.
Metz's captain Sylvain Kastendeuch is also doubtful, while the home side will be without Senegal's Amara Traore, who is away on African Nations' Cup duty.
